text_blocks.snippet: In Texas, "assault causing bodily injury" involves intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causing physical pain, illness, or impairment to another person. This offense can range from a Class A misdemeanor to a third-degree felony, depending on the circumstances. "Bodily injury" is broadly defined, encompassing even minor physical pain or discomfort.
snippet_highlighted_words: intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causing physical pain, illness, or impairment to another person

list.title: Intent:
list.snippet: The prosecution must prove the defendant acted intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly.

list.title: Bodily Injury:
list.snippet: This includes physical pain, illness, or any impairment of physical condition. Even a small scratch, bruise, or a statement of pain can be sufficient.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: While generally a Class A misdemeanor, it can be elevated to a third-degree felony if the victim is a public servant, or if the assault is against a family member and the defendant has a prior conviction.

list.title: Aggravated Assault:
list.snippet: If the assault causes serious bodily injury (creating a substantial risk of death or causing serious permanent disfigurement, etc.) or involves a deadly weapon, it becomes aggravated assault and is a felony.

list.title: Defenses:
list.snippet: Defenses may include lack of intent, accident, or consent (if applicable and doesn't involve serious bodily injury).

text_blocks.snippet: Example: If two people are arguing and one person pushes the other, causing a bruise, this could be considered assault causing bodily injury.

list.snippet: Class A Misdemeanor: Up to one year in jail and a fine of up to $4,000.
Third-Degree Felony: 2-10 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000.
Aggravated Assault: Ranges from 2-20 years in prison for a second-degree felony.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: It's crucial to consult with a legal professional for advice specific to your situation, as the details of each case can significantly impact the charges and potential penalties.
